title: Prefixes & Suffixes
subtitle: Word parts, and reading a word you have never seen.
objectives: Explain what a prefix and a suffix do
Work out a word's meaning from its parts
Use suffixes to change a word's job

cards.title: Most long words are short words with bits attached
cards.text: If you know the parts, you can read a word you have never seen. That is the entire trick.

cards.title: Goes on the front and changes the meaning
cards.text: The root stays. The meaning flips, reverses or shifts.

cards.title: Goes on the end and usually changes the job
cards.text: It can turn a verb into a noun, or a noun into an adjective.
points: **-ly** turns an adjective into an adverb: *quick → quickly*.

cards.title: Front changes meaning, back changes job
cards.text: Six affixes. The split between the two halves is the whole lesson.

question.explain: The prefix over- means too much. The root is unchanged.

cards.title: A teardown is a parade of prefixes
cards.text: Almost every step verb has one, and the prefix tells you the direction of the work.
points: **overheat**: what went wrong in the first place.

question.text: Add one prefix to 'connect' so it means the opposite. Write the whole word.

cards.title: Suffixes decide what you are being called
cards.text: Same root, different ending, different person entirely.
points: **box → boxer**: the one who does it.

cards.title: Break it, then rebuild it
cards.text: Strip the prefix, strip the suffix, look at what is left.
points: **Not + break + able to be** → cannot be broken.
**You never needed a dictionary** for that one.
**Works on most long words** you will meet.

question.explain: A prefix, a root and a suffix. Not + break + able to be.

cards.title: A word is built, not found
cards.alt: Three plastic building blocks clicked together in a row, small, large and small, with visible joins
cards.text: Front piece, root, back piece. You can see every join.

cards.title: Literature Review: Don Quixote, Chapter 16: The Ox-Cart Journey
cards.text: Quixote, bruised and caged, is carried home on an ox-cart, convinced he is enchanted.
points: **He is powerless** and reads it as magic.
**His friends are hopeful** he will recover.
**The word parts carry the mood** of the chapter.

terms.def: A word part added to the front, changing meaning.
A word part added to the end, usually changing the word's job.
The core word before anything is added.
The general name for a prefix or a suffix.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Prefix on the front changes the meaning.
Suffix on the end usually changes the job.
un-, re-, dis-, over- cover a great many words.
Break an unknown word into parts and it usually gives itself up.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 English. The lesson is sold on its payoff rather than its terminology: knowing the parts lets him read an unfamiliar word without help, and 'unbreakable' is worked through as the demonstration. Prefixes and suffixes are separated by function (prefixes change meaning, suffixes change the word's job) which is the distinction an exam tests and which most learners blur. The teardown card is not decoration here: unplug, unscrew, disconnect, reassemble, overheat are genuinely the vocabulary of the activity, so the prefixes arrive already attached to actions.
discussion: What is the difference between what a prefix does and what a suffix does?
How would you read a long word you had never met?
Which prefixes appear in a teardown?
